sources.title: Steven Weinberg, Non-Renormalization Theorems in Non-Renormalizable Theories
sources.locator: Full 13-page PDF fetched. Read the action and Wilsonian form on pp. 1–3; the complete spurion, R-symmetry, theta-shift, and graph-counting proof on pp. 3–7; and the separate Fayet–Iliopoulos argument on p. 8. No continuum construction or arbitrary 1PI result is imported.

searches.query: Steven Weinberg Non-Renormalization Theorems in Non-Renormalizable Theories hep-th/9803099 full text PDF
searches.outcome: Found and opened the complete arXiv PDF; inspected the full perturbative proof, graph-counting argument, and Fayet–Iliopoulos qualification.

contents.name: Perturbative Wilsonian holomorphic F-term nonrenormalization
contents.support: The action definition and equations (3)–(12), pp. 2–7, state the preserved-symmetry form, chiral and real spurions, R and theta-shift restrictions, and the graph count showing that the original holomorphic F integrand is unchanged apart from the one-loop gauge-coupling term.

contents.name: One-loop gauge-coupling exception and Fayet–Iliopoulos charge trace
contents.support: Equation (4), p. 3, identifies the simple-group one-loop gauge-coupling shift. The separate argument on pp. 7–8 shows that the U(1) Fayet–Iliopoulos correction is a one-loop matter tadpole proportional to the sum of chiral charges.

contents.name: Explicit opposite-charge U(1) FI cancellation example
contents.support: The pp. 7–8 tadpole argument gives the exact charge-trace criterion used by the example with one charge +1 and one charge -1 chiral field.

contents.name: Perturbative, Wilsonian, and nonperturbative scope boundary
contents.support: The source distinguishes perturbative Wilsonian F terms from nonperturbative effects and does not identify the Wilsonian action with an arbitrary one-particle-irreducible functional.

contents.name: Matter-vertex multiplicity derived from equation (12)
contents.support: Substitution of the vector-end and R-charge equations gives N_tau = 1 - 1/2[sum(m-2)A_m + sum(m+2-r)B_mr + sum m C_m]. At N_tau=0 the one-vertex m=2 matter case must have C_2=1. The prose immediately after equation (12) appears to print C_2=2; the item uses the value forced by the displayed count equation and records the discrepancy.

sources.title: Stephen P. Martin, A Supersymmetry Primer, version 7
sources.locator: Full 160-page PDF fetched. Read §4.7, printed p. 41, for the chiral superspace action; §4.10, printed pp. 48–49, for general holomorphic superpotential, Kähler, and gauge-kinetic data; and §6.5, printed pp. 66–67, for wave-function anomalous dimensions and the superpotential renormalization-group equations.

searches.query: Stephen Martin Supersymmetry Primer nonrenormalization theorem section 6.5 PDF
searches.outcome: Found the author's version-7 full lecture notes and inspected the superspace action, nonrenormalizable-action, and renormalization-group sections.

contents.name: Supersymmetric action data and the distinction between holomorphic and real superspace terms
contents.support: Sections 4.7 and 4.10 give the chiral-superfield action, arbitrary holomorphic superpotential, real Kähler potential, and holomorphic gauge-kinetic function used to define the local perturbative action data.

contents.name: Wave-function renormalization and running canonical couplings
contents.support: Section 6.5 gives superpotential beta functions in terms of chiral-superfield anomalous dimensions, corroborating that the unrenormalized holomorphic Wilsonian coefficient can differ from a canonically normalized running coupling.

contents.name: F-term protection does not imply Kähler or D-term protection
contents.support: Sections 4.10 and 6.5 distinguish real Kähler data and wave-function effects from the holomorphic superpotential nonrenormalization statement.
